panels.title: PostgreSQL
panels.description: Can postgres-exporter connect to the server?

panels.title: Up for
panels.description: Time since the server (postmaster) started.

panels.title: Connections used
panels.description: All server connections (every database) as % of max_connections. Near 100% = new clients get 'too many connections'.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of data pages served from memory (shared buffers) instead of disk. Healthy OLTP: above 99%.

panels.title: Transactions / sec
panels.description: Committed + rolled back. Every statement outside BEGIN/COMMIT is its own transaction.

panels.title: Transactions OK
panels.description: Committed / all transactions. A failing SQL statement rolls its transaction back.

panels.title: SQL OK (app, range)
panels.description: SQL commands the app ran successfully in the selected time range (Npgsql client metrics).

panels.title: SQL failed (app, range)
panels.description: SQL commands that returned an error to the app (syntax, missing table, timeout, lost connection...).

panels.title: Rows written / sec
panels.description: Inserted + updated + deleted rows.

panels.title: Deadlocks (range)
panels.description: Transactions PostgreSQL had to kill because they waited on each other.

panels.title: Commits vs rollbacks / sec
panels.description: Rollbacks mean failed statements or an explicit ROLLBACK.

panels.title: SQL from the app (Npgsql client metrics) - successful vs failed
SQL commands / sec: OK vs failed
panels.description: What the app saw. Failed = the command returned an error (see logs / trace for which one).

panels.title: SQL latency P50 / P95 / P99 (dots = exemplars -> trace)
panels.description: Time per SQL command as measured by the app, network included.

panels.title: Server connections by state
panels.description: active = running a query; idle = connected, waiting (pooled); idle in transaction = transaction open but doing nothing (holds locks - should be ~0).

panels.title: Server connections by user
panels.description: lab = the app, rootprint = Rootprint, postgres_exporter = monitoring.

panels.title: App connection pool (Npgsql)
panels.description: The app keeps connections open (idle) and reuses them; used hitting max = requests wait for a connection.

panels.title: Rows read / sec
panels.description: Returned much higher than fetched = many rows scanned to find few - a missing index.

panels.title: Cache hit % and temp files
panels.description: Below ~99% the working set does not fit in shared_buffers.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: accesssharelock = plain SELECTs; rowexclusivelock = INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; exclusive modes block others.

panels.title: Longest open transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction per connection state. Long ones block VACUUM and hold locks (try /diagnostics/problem/slow-db).

panels.title: Tables (now)
panels.description: Seq/index scans are for the selected range. Many seq scans on a big table = a query without a usable index.

panels.title: Heaviest queries in the selected range (by total time)
panels.description: Total time = calls x mean time: the queries worth optimising first. Parameters are shown as $1, $2.

targets.expr: topk(5, sum by (queryid) (rate(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname=~"$db"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (queryid) group_left (query) max by (queryid, query) (pg_stat_statements_query_id{job="postgres"})

panels.title: Top 5 queries by time spent (s per s)
panels.description: Seconds of execution per second of wall time - 1.0 = one connection busy all the time with this query.

targets.expr: topk(5, sum by (queryid) (rate(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname=~"$db"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (queryid) group_left (query) max by (queryid, query) (pg_stat_statements_query_id{job="postgres"})

options.content:
- **Two views of the same database.** *Server side* (postgres-exporter: transactions, connections, locks, tables, pg_stat_statements) and *app side* (Npgsql: what the app saw - OK vs failed SQL, latency, its connection pool).
- **Is it healthy?** PostgreSQL *UP*, *Connections used* well below 100%, *Cache hit ratio* > 99%, *Transactions OK* ~100%, *SQL failed* 0, no *Deadlocks*, *Longest open transaction* in milliseconds.
- **Failed SQL**: `curl localhost:8080/diagnostics/problem/db-error` (missing table) → *SQL failed* and *rollbacks* go up; the error with its trace is in Rootprint logs (`severity_text:Error`).
- **Slow SQL / long transaction**: `curl "localhost:8080/diagnostics/problem/slow-db?seconds=5"` → *SQL latency* and *Longest open transaction* jump; the query shows up in *Heaviest queries*.
- **Connections**: `idle` = pooled connections waiting (normal); `idle in transaction` staying above 0 = a transaction left open (holds locks, blocks VACUUM).
- **Which query is expensive?** *Heaviest queries* - sorted by total time (calls × mean). High calls with low mean = chatty code (N+1); low calls with high mean = a query to tune (EXPLAIN ANALYZE).
- Data: `pg_stat_database`, `pg_stat_activity`, `pg_locks`, `pg_stat_user_tables`, `pg_stat_statements` (enabled with `shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements`).
